raw_response:
I am 63 this year. My wife and I have worked these 15 mu for 40 years. I only finished primary school, so I do not read books about farming. I do what I have always done, and I watch the neighbors. Last year my wheat gave about 900 jin per mu and the maize gave over 1,000 jin per mu, so I will not change much.

For the 12 mu of wheat already in the ground since last autumn, I sowed the same improved seed as my neighbor Zhang — about 25 jin per mu. At sowing time I put one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer into every mu. Now that spring is here, I will topdress with one 80-jin bag of urea at green-up. That is plenty. I will pump water from my well three times: green-up, jointing, and when the grain is filling. Electricity costs money, but three times is what I have always done. I will spray twice for bugs. I expect 450 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After we harvest the wheat in June, I will plant hybrid maize on those same 12 mu. I hire the machine to chop the wheat straw and direct-seed the maize right into the stubble — there is no time to plow between harvest and sowing, and everyone does it this way now. I give maize one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer at sowing and one 80-jin bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations, two sprays. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

I keep 3 mu of cotton because the price is decent, but it is hard work for two old people. I plough deep in spring and sow the improved seed from the red bag — the same one I bought last year. I spread half an 80-jin bag of urea and half a 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Cotton needs water at flowering and when the bolls are growing, so three irrigations. I spray three times because aphids and red spiders always show up. I hope for 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer costs more this year, but I would rather spend the money than lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting a little fertilizer is just money down the well. I do what my neighbors do, and this is what we all do around here.
